title: What is smile design and who is it for?
desc: What smile design is, which treatments it can include, who it suits, how the trial stage works and what affects the cost.
lead: Smile design is a planning method that sets the length, shape and colour of the teeth and the gum line according to your facial proportions, and lets you see the result before treatment begins.

sections.h: What exactly does smile design involve?
sections.html:
Smile design is not a single procedure but a way of planning. First, your face, lips and teeth are examined as a whole: how much tooth shows when you talk and smile, your facial midline, the gum level and the proportions between teeth.

This is recorded with photos, video and an intraoral scan. The intended result is then designed digitally. The design works like a prescription: it shows which tooth needs which treatment — and where nothing should be done at all.

sections.h: Who is it suitable for, and who is it not?
sections.html:
Smile design usually makes sense for people with more than one aesthetic concern who want to solve them in a single plan:

  • The length, shape or colour of the teeth looks out of balance with the face
  • There are gaps, chips or worn edges
  • Too much gum shows when smiling, or the gum line is uneven
  • Old crowns and fillings no longer match in colour

Untreated decay, gum disease or a significant bite problem must be dealt with first. An aesthetic plan is built on a healthy foundation.

sections.h: How does the process work, step by step?
sections.html:
The table below gives a general framework. The exact timeline depends on which treatments the plan includes and is set after the examination.

StageWhat happensTypical time
Examination and recordsClinical exam, X-rays, photos, video and scan1 appointment
Digital designPlanning target tooth length, shape and proportionsA few days
Trial (mock-up)Trying the design in the mouth with temporary material1 appointment
TreatmentTreatments according to the approved planDepends on the treatment chosen
ReviewFit, bite and maintenance check1 appointment
Why the trial stage matters

With a mock-up you see the result on your own face, in the mirror. Any detail you don't like is changed before anything permanent is done.

sections.h: Which treatments can be part of smile design?
sections.html:
The plan is shaped around you. For some patients whitening and a little bonding are enough; others need a combination of treatments:

  • Teeth whitening: to lighten natural teeth
  • Orthodontics / clear aligners: to align crowded teeth without reducing them
  • Laminate veneers: thin porcelain layers to change shape and colour
  • Zirconia crowns: for teeth with more tissue loss
  • Gum contouring: to balance the gum line

Smile design does not always mean reducing teeth. The least invasive option that preserves the natural tooth should always be considered first.

There is no single price for smile design; the cost follows the content of the plan. Getting an itemised written plan after the examination is the soundest way to compare.

FactorEffect on cost
Number of teeth treatedA plan for 6, 8 or 10 visible teeth costs differently
Material chosenVeneers, zirconia or bonding differ in cost and lifespan
Preliminary treatmentOrthodontics, gum treatment or decay treatment may be needed
Laboratory and digital workflowCustom design and trial stages are part of the plan

faq.q: Is smile design painful?
faq.a: The design and trial stages are painless. Treatments that require tooth preparation are done under local anaesthetic; there may be short-term sensitivity afterwards.

faq.q: Can I see the result in advance?
faq.a: Yes. With the digital design and an in-mouth trial (mock-up), you see the result on your own face before any permanent work.

faq.q: Do my teeth have to be reduced?
faq.a: No. The plan may consist of non-invasive treatments such as whitening, orthodontics or bonding. If reduction is needed, the reason and amount are explained before starting.

faq.q: How long does the result last?
faq.a: It depends on the treatments used, oral hygiene and habits. Porcelain restorations can last many years; regular check-ups extend their life.

title: All-on-Four: are fixed teeth on four implants really possible?
desc: What All-on-Four is, who it suits and whether same-day fixed teeth are possible. The process, risks, limitations and cost factors.
lead: All-on-Four is a treatment in which a fixed full-arch prosthesis is placed on four implants in a jaw that has no teeth or is about to lose them.

sections.html:
In a conventional approach, six to eight implants may be planned for a full jaw. All-on-Four uses four: the two front implants are placed upright and the two back implants at an angle.

The angled back implants take support from areas where the bone is denser. This keeps them away from the sinus in the upper jaw and the nerve in the lower jaw, which reduces the need for bone grafting in many patients.

• People missing all teeth in one jaw
  • People whose remaining teeth cannot be saved because of advanced gum disease
  • Denture wearers who want fixed teeth
  • Patients whose CT scan shows enough bone for four implants

Uncontrolled diabetes, heavy smoking, a history of head and neck radiotherapy and certain bone medications increase the risk. These should be discussed in detail at the examination.

If the implants achieve enough initial stability (primary stability) in the bone, most patients can have a temporary fixed prosthesis fitted the same day or within a few days, so you are not left without teeth while healing.

The temporary prosthesis is used until the bone has fused with the implants. A soft diet is needed in the first weeks. The final prosthesis is made from new impressions after healing.

Note

If initial stability is not sufficient, the dentist may let the implants heal without load. This decision is made during surgery, based on the bone.

sections.h: How are the process and timeline planned?
sections.html:
StageTypical time
Examination and 3D CT scan1–2 appointments
Any extractions, implant surgery and temporary fixed prosthesisUsually the same day or within a few days
Healing and bone integrationAbout 3–6 months
Making and fitting the final prosthesisSeveral appointments
Check-ups and professional cleaningAt least 1–2 times a year

These are general ranges; they vary with bone quality and general health.

sections.h: What are the risks and limitations?
sections.html:
When well planned, All-on-Four is a predictable treatment, but like any implant treatment it carries risks:

  • An implant failing to integrate with the bone (more common with smoking and uncontrolled diabetes)
  • Inflammation around implants (peri-implantitis), mostly linked to inadequate cleaning
  • Fracture or wear of the prosthesis in people who clench or grind at night
  • The prosthesis needing maintenance or renewal in the long term

The underside of a fixed prosthesis must be cleaned too. Interdental brushes and a water flosser should be part of the daily routine, as your dentist will show you.

FactorExplanation
Implant systemClinical evidence and long-term parts availability matter
Final prosthesis materialAcrylic, composite or zirconia differ in cost and durability
Additional proceduresExtractions or limited bone grafting may be needed
One or two jawsEach jaw is planned separately

faq.q: Can four implants carry all the teeth?
faq.a: With suitable bone and correct planning, yes. Angled back implants spread the load over a wider area. If bone is insufficient, more implants may be recommended.

faq.q: Will the surgery hurt?
faq.a: It is done under local anaesthetic; sedation can be discussed if you wish. Swelling and tenderness may follow for a few days and are managed with prescribed medication.

faq.q: Can I eat normally with temporary teeth?
faq.a: A soft diet is recommended for the first weeks. Hard and sticky food can overload the implants until the bone has integrated.

faq.q: Can the All-on-Four prosthesis be removed?
faq.a: Not by the patient. Because it is screw-retained, the dentist can remove it for cleaning at check-ups.

faq.q: Is All-on-Four suitable for everyone?
faq.a: No. A decision can't be made without a CT scan and an assessment of general health and bone volume. For some patients a conventional implant plan is better.

title: What are laminate veneers, are teeth reduced, and how long do they last?
desc: What laminate veneers are, how much tooth is reduced, who they suit and how long they last. Comparison with zirconia and the process.
lead: A laminate veneer is a thin layer of porcelain, usually 0.3–0.7 mm thick, bonded only to the front surface of a tooth.

sections.html:
In most cases a very thin layer of enamel is removed from the front of the tooth, usually less than half a millimetre. The aim is for the porcelain to create a natural profile without bulging.

In some cases — for example when teeth are small or set back — veneers can be placed without any reduction (no-prep). But this does not suit every tooth and can lead to a bulky look and gum problems.

Important

Removed enamel does not grow back. The decision for veneers should be made after alternatives (whitening, orthodontics, bonding) have been discussed.

• Discolouration that does not respond to whitening
  • Small chips and wear on front teeth
  • Small gaps between teeth
  • Mismatched shape and length

With severe crowding, heavy clenching or when most of the tooth is missing, veneers may not be a good option. In those cases orthodontics or crowns are considered.

FeatureLaminate veneerZirconia crown
CoverageFront surface of the toothAll surfaces of the tooth
Tooth tissue removedLittleMore
Suitable forSound front teeth without large fillingsWeakened, root-treated or fractured teeth
TranslucencyVery highHigh

In short, veneers are for teeth that are structurally sound and whose appearance you mainly want to change. If a tooth is weakened, a crown protects it better.

Studies report that most porcelain veneers placed for the right indication with good bonding technique remain in place for ten years or more.

The main factors that shorten their life are night-time clenching, nail biting or biting hard objects, poor oral hygiene and gum recession. If you clench, a night guard is recommended.

StageWhat happensTypical time
PlanningPhotos, scan and smile design1 appointment
TrialTrying the design temporarily in the mouth1 appointment
Preparation and impressionsAny minimal reduction and impressions1 appointment
BondingPermanent bonding after colour and fit checks1 appointment

Including laboratory time, the process is usually completed within one to two weeks.

FactorExplanation
Number of teethPlanned according to how many teeth show in your smile
Porcelain type and laboratoryLayered or monolithic porcelain, hand finishing
Preliminary treatmentWhitening, gum contouring or orthodontics may be needed

faq.q: Will my teeth be sensitive after veneers?
faq.a: There may be short-term sensitivity. Because reduction stays within the enamel, lasting sensitivity is rare.

faq.q: Do veneers change colour?
faq.a: Porcelain does not stain or change colour. Natural teeth can darken over time, so if whitening is needed it is done before the veneers.

faq.q: Can a veneer come off?
faq.a: It is rare when bonded correctly. Biting hard objects and clenching increase the risk.

faq.q: Can veneers be removed so I go back to my old teeth?
faq.a: If teeth were reduced, the surface does not return to its original state; the tooth should always be protected by a restoration. This is worth knowing before you decide.

title: Teeth whitening: in the clinic or at home? How long does it last?
desc: The differences between in-clinic and at-home whitening, how long results last, sensitivity and cases where whitening doesn't work.
lead: Teeth whitening is a dentist-supervised procedure that lightens tooth colour by breaking down pigments in the enamel and dentine with peroxide-based gels.

sections.h: What is the difference between in-clinic and at-home whitening?
sections.html:
Both methods use the same active ingredient; the difference is gel concentration and application time.

MethodHow it's appliedTypical timeWho it suits
In-clinic (in-office)Gums are protected; a high-concentration gel is applied by the dentistOne session, about 1–1.5 hoursThose who want a quick result
At home (with trays)Low-concentration gel in custom-made traysUsually 1–2 weeks of daily useThose who want gradual, controlled lightening
CombinedStart in the clinic, continue at homeOne clinic session + short home useThose who want a more pronounced, even result

Over-the-counter products are usually very low in concentration, and because the trays aren't custom-made the gel can reach the gums. Dentist-supervised whitening gives more predictable results.

The result is not permanent; teeth gradually pick up colour again. How quickly depends on habits. Tea, coffee, red wine and smoking bring the colour back faster.

Most patients notice the effect for one to several years. If you keep your home trays, short top-up applications can be done on your dentist's advice.

sections.h: Does it cause sensitivity or damage enamel?
sections.html:
Temporary sensitivity is a common side effect and usually settles on its own within a few days. Desensitising toothpaste and adjusting application intervals help.

Studies have shown that whitening at recommended concentrations under a dentist's supervision does not permanently damage enamel. The real risk is uncontrolled, excessive use.

Examination first

Decay, exposed root surfaces or leaking fillings can make whitening painful. That's why an examination and scale-and-polish come first.

• Crowns, fillings and veneers: restorations don't whiten, so a colour mismatch may appear afterwards.
  • Some medication-related staining: for example, tetracycline stains respond only partly.
  • Dark root-treated teeth: special internal whitening may be needed.

In these cases options such as veneers or crowns are discussed.

sections.h: What should I watch out for after whitening?
sections.html:
• Avoid tea, coffee, cola, red wine and coloured sauces for the first 48 hours.
  • Try not to smoke during this time.
  • If teeth are sensitive, cut down on very hot and very cold food for a few days.
  • Check-ups and cleaning every six months help keep the colour.

faq.q: How many shades lighter will my teeth get?
faq.a: It depends on the starting colour and type of staining. Yellowish teeth usually respond well; greyish discolouration lightens less.

faq.q: Can I whiten my teeth while pregnant?
faq.a: Whitening is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding; it is best postponed until afterwards.

faq.q: Is whitening painful?
faq.a: No pain is expected during the procedure. Some patients have temporary sensitivity and brief twinges.

faq.q: Will my crowns whiten too?
faq.a: No. Porcelain and zirconia restorations don't change colour. If you have restorations on front teeth, colour matching should be planned in advance.

title: Travelling to Istanbul for dental treatment: a planning guide
desc: Coming to Istanbul for dental treatment from abroad: what to send in advance, how long to stay, planning the trip and aftercare at home.
lead: If you are thinking of coming to Istanbul from abroad for dental treatment, the most important step is to settle the treatment plan and length of stay before you book a flight.

sections.h: What should I send before I come?
sections.html:
The more detailed the preliminary assessment, the more realistic the plan. You can send the following via WhatsApp:

  • A panoramic X-ray taken within the last 6 months (and a CT scan if you have one)
  • Clear photos of your teeth from the front, the side and while smiling
  • Any medication you take and chronic conditions
  • Your expectations: what you want to change and what bothers you

With this, the dentist prepares a preliminary plan. The final plan can only be confirmed after an examination and imaging at the clinic — it's important to know this before you travel.

sections.h: How long will I need to stay?
sections.html:
The length of stay varies a lot by treatment. The figures below are general ranges:

TreatmentFirst visitSecond visit
Zirconia / veneersAbout 5–7 daysUsually not needed
Implants (final teeth later)2–5 daysAfter 3–6 months, about 5–7 days
All-on-FourAbout 5–7 days (temporary fixed teeth)After 3–6 months, for the final prosthesis
Teeth whitening1–2 daysNot needed
Clear aligners1–3 days to startRemote follow-up + periodic check-ups
Flexible return

Book a flexible return flight if you can. Small adjustments at the trial stage may need a day or two more.

sections.h: How should I plan the trip?
sections.html:
Dent32 is in Beylikdüzü, on the European side of Istanbul. Staying on the European side makes clinic visits easier; Istanbul Airport is closer to this area than Sabiha Gökçen.

  • If you are having surgery, don't plan a busy sightseeing day for the same day.
  • Ask your dentist about flight timing after implant surgery or extractions.
  • Alcohol and smoking slow healing on treatment days.
  • Bring any medication you take regularly.

sections.h: How does follow-up work once I'm home?
sections.html:
Your X-rays and records are given to you after treatment, so your dentist at home can see what was done. During healing, you can reach your dentist via WhatsApp by sending photos with your questions.

In the long run, most of the success depends on maintenance. A check-up and professional cleaning at least once a year should not be skipped, wherever it is done.

Comparing quotes from different clinics on the total figure alone can be misleading. Ask these questions:

TopicQuestion to ask
MaterialsWhich implant brand, and which type of zirconia or porcelain, will be used?
ScopeAre X-rays, CT scans, temporary teeth and check-ups included?
Number of teethWhich teeth does the plan cover, and why?
AlternativesIs there a less invasive option?

faq.q: Can I communicate in English?
faq.a: Yes. You can communicate in English during the preliminary assessment and appointment process.

faq.q: Can I get a firm price from photos?
faq.a: Photos and X-rays allow preliminary information; the final plan and cost are confirmed after the examination at the clinic.

faq.q: Can I have the implant and the final tooth in the same visit?
faq.a: In most cases, no. The implant needs a few months to integrate with the bone. In some cases temporary fixed teeth can be fitted.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book?
faq.a: Complete the preliminary assessment before booking flights, then agree dates with the clinic so treatment days fit your trip.

faq.q: What if there's a problem after treatment?
faq.a: Send photos and a description via WhatsApp. The dentist will assess the situation and advise you.

title: Clear aligners or braces? The real differences between them
desc: Clear aligners versus fixed braces: appearance, comfort, suitable cases, treatment time and retention afterwards.
lead: Clear aligners and fixed braces are two orthodontic methods for straightening teeth; both are effective, but they differ in appearance, the discipline they require and the cases they suit.

sections.html:
FeatureClear alignersFixed braces
VisibilityAlmost invisibleVisible (clear brackets are an option)
RemovabilityRemoved for eating and brushingFixed; removed by the orthodontist
Patient complianceMust be worn 20–22 hours a dayDoesn't depend on the patient wearing them
Oral hygieneBrushing is easyBrackets need extra care
Food restrictionsFew, since aligners come outAvoid hard and sticky food
Complex casesCan be limitedWider control of tooth movement

sections.h: When are braces the better choice?
sections.html:
Clear aligners have improved a great deal and work well in many cases. Even so, fixed braces are more predictable in some situations:

  • Severe crowding or cases that require extractions
  • Cases needing significant vertical tooth movement
  • Skeletal problems arising from the jaw relationship
  • Patients who don't think they can wear aligners for the recommended hours
What decides it?

The right method is chosen after an examination, X-rays and an intraoral scan. A comparative recommendation from an orthodontist who uses both methods is the soundest route.

For cases of similar difficulty, the two methods usually take a similar time. What determines duration is not the method but how far, and in which direction, the teeth need to move.

Mild cases can be completed in a few months, while comprehensive treatment can take one to two years. With aligners, the most common cause of delay is not wearing them long enough.

sections.h: How do they compare for pain and comfort?
sections.html: With both methods, a feeling of pressure for a few days after a new aligner or wire adjustment is normal. With fixed braces, brackets can rub the cheeks and lips and cause sores in the first weeks; orthodontic wax helps. Aligners cause less of this irritation.

Teeth tend to drift back towards their old positions. That's why both methods end with a retention phase: a thin wire bonded behind the teeth, a clear retainer worn at night, or both.

Neglecting the retainer is the most common reason results deteriorate after orthodontics.

FactorExplanation
Case complexityAmount of tooth movement needed and number of aligners
Treatment length and number of visitsLonger treatment needs more appointments
Aligner system / bracket typeMetal, clear brackets or different aligner systems
RetainersThe retention plan after treatment

faq.q: Do aligners affect speech?
faq.a: There may be a slight lisp for the first few days; most patients adapt quickly.

faq.q: Can I eat with aligners in?
faq.a: No. Take them out for anything other than water, then brush and put them back in.

faq.q: Can adults have orthodontic treatment?
faq.a: Yes. As long as gums and bone are healthy, age alone is not a barrier.

faq.q: Which is faster, braces or aligners?
faq.a: For similar cases the times are close. With aligners, the duration depends largely on wearing them consistently.

title: Zirconia or porcelain? What to consider when choosing a crown
desc: Zirconia versus porcelain-fused-to-metal crowns: aesthetics, strength, gum compatibility, lifespan and the process.
lead: Zirconia and porcelain-fused-to-metal are two common types of dental crown; the key difference is whether the framework underneath is metal or zirconia ceramic.

sections.h: What is the difference between them?
sections.html:
FeatureZirconiaPorcelain-fused-to-metal
FrameworkZirconia ceramic (no metal)Porcelain over a metal alloy
TranslucencyHigh, natural lookMore opaque because of the metal
Gum marginNo dark lineA dark edge may show if gums recede
StrengthVery highHigh, with a long clinical track record
Tissue compatibilityHighly biocompatibleMay not suit people with metal allergies

sections.h: Which is better for front teeth?
sections.html:
Because appearance is the priority for front teeth, metal-free options are usually preferred. Zirconia transmits light much like a natural tooth and doesn't cast a shadow at the gum line.

If the tooth is sound and only its appearance needs changing, options that remove less tooth tissue — such as laminate veneers or glass ceramics (e.max) — are also considered instead of a full crown.

sections.h: Which is better for back teeth?
sections.html:
Back teeth take high chewing forces. Monolithic (single-piece) zirconia is very resistant to fracture in this area. Porcelain-fused-to-metal has also been used successfully in the back of the mouth for many years.

The choice takes into account the opposing teeth, any clenching habit and the gum level.

Well-planned, correctly placed crowns serve most patients for many years; ten years or more is common. The main factor in their lifespan is usually not the material but oral hygiene.

  • Cleaning between teeth is essential to prevent decay at the crown margin.
  • If you clench, wear a night guard.
  • Regular check-ups monitor margin fit and gum health.
Reminder

The tooth under a crown is either vital or root-treated; in both cases it can still decay. A crown protects the tooth but does not replace good hygiene.

sections.h: How does the crown process work?
sections.html:
StageWhat happensTypical time
ExaminationX-rays; root canal or gum treatment if needed1 appointment
Preparation and impressionsTooth preparation, digital or conventional impressions, temporaries1 appointment
Try-inFit, colour and bite check1 appointment
CementationPermanent cementation and final check1 appointment

Including laboratory time, most patients complete the process in about a week; it takes longer if preliminary treatment is needed.

FactorExplanation
MaterialMonolithic or layered zirconia, porcelain-fused-to-metal
Number of teethSingle crown, bridge or full-mouth plan
Preliminary treatmentRoot canal treatment, fillings, gum treatment
Laboratory workHand finishing for colour and form matching

faq.q: How much are teeth reduced for zirconia crowns?
faq.a: Because a crown covers all surfaces, a certain amount of tooth is reduced. The amount depends on the material and the tooth; your dentist explains it before starting.

faq.q: Does zirconia change colour?
faq.a: No. Zirconia and porcelain don't stain. Neighbouring natural teeth can change colour over time, though.

faq.q: Will the crowned tooth hurt?
faq.a: The procedure is done under local anaesthetic. There may be hot and cold sensitivity for a few days afterwards.

faq.q: I have a metal allergy — which should I choose?
faq.a: Metal-free zirconia or all-ceramic options are suitable.

title: What is implant treatment and how many months does it really take?
desc: What implant treatment is, its stages and how long it really takes. What extends the timeline, same-day implants and cost factors.
lead: Implant treatment replaces the root of a missing tooth with a titanium screw placed in the jawbone, topped with a permanent tooth; for most patients the whole process takes between 3 and 6 months.

sections.h: What is an implant and how does it work?
sections.html:
An implant is a small screw placed in the jawbone that takes over the role of a natural tooth root. It is usually made of titanium or a titanium alloy, a material that can fuse directly with bone. This fusion is called osseointegration.

Once integration is complete, a connector (abutment) is attached to the implant and a crown, bridge or prosthesis is fixed on top. Replacing a missing tooth without touching the neighbouring teeth is the implant's main advantage over a bridge.

sections.h: How many months does treatment really take?
sections.html:
Most of the time is the waiting period needed for the implant to integrate with the bone. The table below shows general ranges:

StageTypical time
Examination and 3D CT scan1–2 appointments
Healing after extraction (if needed)About 2–3 months, or implant placed at the same visit
Bone graft / sinus lift (if needed)Can add 3–6 months
Placing the implantUsually 30–60 minutes for a single implant
Bone integrationAbout 2–3 months in the lower jaw, 3–6 months in the upper
Impressions and final toothA few appointments, about 1–2 weeks
In short

In a patient with enough healthy bone, a single implant can be completed in about 3–4 months. If bone grafting is needed, the total can extend to 6–9 months.

• Insufficient bone volume: a bone graft or sinus lift may be needed.
  • Active infection: inflammation in the tooth or gum is treated first.
  • Smoking: slows healing and increases the risk of failure.
  • Uncontrolled diabetes and some medications: can affect bone healing.
  • Upper jaw: bone is usually less dense, so integration takes longer.

sections.h: Are same-day implants and teeth possible?
sections.html:
In some cases an implant can be placed at the same visit as the extraction (immediate implant). If initial stability is sufficient, a temporary tooth can be fitted the same day. That temporary tooth is adjusted so it takes no chewing load; the final tooth is still made after integration.

This approach is not suitable for every patient. Bone structure, infection and tooth position are assessed together.

Implant placement is done under local anaesthetic, and most patients feel no pain during the procedure, though pressure and vibration may be felt. Mild swelling and tenderness for a few days afterwards are normal and are managed with painkillers.

In the first days, cold compresses, a soft diet and gentle cleaning of the area are recommended.

FactorExplanation
Implant brandSystems with strong clinical evidence and long-term parts availability are preferable
RestorationZirconia or porcelain-fused-to-metal crown
Additional surgeryBone graft, sinus lift, extraction
Number of implantsSingle tooth, bridge or full-mouth plan

faq.q: Do implants last a lifetime?
faq.a: With proper care an implant can last for many years. The crown on top can wear and may need replacing. Regular check-ups and cleaning are the key to success.

faq.q: Can anyone have implants?
faq.a: Most people whose jaw has finished growing, whose health allows minor surgery and who have enough bone can. Some systemic conditions and medications need detailed assessment.

faq.q: What if the implant fails?
faq.a: Rarely, an implant may not integrate. It is then removed and, once the area has healed, a new placement can be planned.

faq.q: When can I go back to work after an implant?
faq.a: Most patients return to daily activities the day after a single implant. After more extensive surgery a few days' rest may be advised.

faq.q: Implant or bridge?
faq.a: An implant doesn't touch neighbouring teeth; a bridge requires them to be reduced. The decision is made by considering bone, general health and expectations together.
